'''Alembic Pharmaceuticals''' is an Indian multinational [[Medication|pharmaceutical]] company headquartered in [[Vadodara|Vadodara, Gujarat]]. The company manufactures and markets pharmaceutical products, including [[Active ingredient|active pharmaceutical ingredients]] (APIs) and formulations, and has a presence in the [[macrolide]] anti-infective drug segment.

Alembic Pharmaceuticals produces formulations for therapeutic areas such as cardiology, dermatology, diabetes, ophthalmology, and infectious diseases for domestic and international markets. It operates manufacturing facilities in [[Gujarat]] (Panelav and Karakhadi), [[Sikkim]], and [[Pithampur]] as well as [[research and development]] centres in India and the United States.

== History ==
Alembic Chemical Works Company Ltd. was established in 1907 in [[Vadodara]], [[Vadodara|Gujarat]], initially producing [[Tincture|tinctures]] and alcohol. It later diversified into cough syrups, vitamins, tonics, and sulphur drugs. In the 1960s, the company began producing [[penicillin]], with its plant inaugurated in 1961 by then Prime Minister [[Lal Bahadur Shastri]]. Bulk production of [[B vitamins|vitamin B{{sub|12}}]] and [[erythromycin]] started in 1971. In 1999, the company changed its name from Alembic Chemical Works Company Ltd. to Alembic Ltd.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Alembic Pharma: Pranav and Shaunak Amin are running the show with an innovation-led approach |url=https://www.forbesindia.com/article/take-one-big-story-of-the-day/alembic-pharma-shaking-things-up/88227/1 |access-date=2025-11-18 |website=www.forbesindia.com |language=en}}</ref>

In 2007, Alembic Ltd. acquired the non-oncology formulation business of Dabur Pharma Ltd for ₹159 crore.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Mukherjee |first=Writankar |date=2007-02-08 |title=Alembic targets lifestyle drug firm |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/healthcare/biotech/pharmaceuticals/alembic-targets-lifestyle-drug-firm/articleshow/1577915.cms?from=mdr |access-date=2025-11-18 |work=The Economic Times |issn=0013-0389}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=How the Amin family scions changed Alembic's fortunes |url=https://www.forbesindia.com/article/super-50-companies-2016/how-the-amin-family-scions-changed-alembics-fortunes/43951/1 |access-date=2025-12-24 |website=www.forbesindia.com |language=en}}</ref>

In 2010, Alembic Pharmaceuticals was formed after a demerger from Alembic Ltd. The demerger was carried out through the allotment of 133,515,914 equity shares of ₹2 each to Alembic Ltd. shareholders, reducing Alembic Ltd.’s stake to 29.18%.  Shares of Alembic Pharmaceuticals were listed on the [[Bombay Stock Exchange]] and [[National Stock Exchange of India|National Stock Exchange]] on 20 September 2011, following the demerger.<ref name=":0" />

In 2014, Alembic Pharmaceuticals formed a joint venture with Adwiya Mami SARL to enter [[Algeria]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alembic forms JV with Adwiya Mami to enter Algerian market |url=https://www.business-standard.com/content/b2b-pharma/alembic-forms-jv-with-adwiya-mami-to-enter-algerian-market-114102700736_1.html |website=Business Standard}}</ref> In 2017, the company acquired Orit Laboratories LLC. USA.<ref name=":0" /> In 2019, it entered the Chinese market through a joint venture.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alembic Pharma forms JV to enter a difficult $100 bn Chinese market |url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/companies/alembic-pharma-forms-jv-to-enter-a-difficult-100-bn-chinese-market-119050700826_1.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240602235814/https://www.business-standard.com/article/companies/alembic-pharma-forms-jv-to-enter-a-difficult-100-bn-chinese-market-119050700826_1.html |archive-date=2 June 2024 |access-date=2025-11-18 |website=www.business-standard.com |language=en-US |url-status=live }}</ref>

In 2022, Alembic Pharmaceuticals acquired 100% stake in Aleor Dermaceuticals Ltd. and merged it with the company.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-03-29 |title=Alembic Pharmaceuticals acquires 100% stake in Aleor Dermaceuticals - BusinessToday |url=https://www.businesstoday.in/industry/pharma/story/alembic-pharmaceuticals-acquires-100-stake-in-aleor-dermaceuticals-327782-2022-03-29 |access-date=2025-11-18 |website=Business Today |language=en}}</ref><ref name=":2" /> In 2025, the U.S. subsidiary of Alembic Pharmaceuticals acquired Utility Therapeutics Ltd, which produces the urinary tract infection drug Pivya (pivmecillinam 185 mg), for US$12 million.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alembic Pharma |url=https://trendlyne-media-mumbai-new.s3.amazonaws.com/uploaded-documents/fundamental/92/64e18622fb7341a9a291e01477589676-05112025.pdf?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=AKIAUABWFMACZL6M6VIP%2F20251118%2Fap-south-1%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20251118T131248Z&X-Amz-Expires=7200&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=c25c0b00ba98cae4d71dabe18501a66e5e7c301b74143aaf6fd15038cc1e26cb |website=ICICI Securities}}</ref>

== Regulatory approvals ==
Between 2024 and 2025, Alembic Pharmaceuticals obtained multiple final and tentative approvals from the [[Food and Drug Administration|United States Food and Drug Administration]] (US FDA) for generic medicines. In December 2024, the company received tentative approval for Olopatadine Hydrochloride Ophthalmic Solution 0.7%, a generic version of ''[[Olopatadine|Pataday Once Daily Relief]]''.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-12-04 |title=Alembic Pharmaceuticals secures tentative USFDA nod for generic eye drops - CNBC TV18 |url=https://www.cnbctv18.com/market/stocks/alembic-pharmaceuticals-share-price-secures-tentative-usfda-approval-for-olopatadine-hydrochloride-solution-19519281.htm |access-date=2025-11-18 |website=CNBCTV18 |language=en}}</ref> This was followed by final approval for [[Rivaroxaban]] tablets in strengths of 2.5 mg, 10 mg, 15 mg, and 20 mg, therapeutically equivalent to ''Xarelto'' in May 2025, and for Amlodipine and Atorvastatin tablets in multiple strengths, equivalent to ''Caduet''.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Deva |first=Pranati |date=2025-06-30 |title=Alembic Pharma surges over 12% on USFDA approval for Cancer drug {{!}} Stock Market News |url=https://www.livemint.com/market/stock-market-news/alembic-pharma-surges-over-12-on-usfda-approval-for-cancer-drug-11751258142994.html |access-date=2025-11-18 |website=mint |language=en}}</ref> In June 2025, Alembic Pharmaceuticals received final approval for Doxorubicin Hydrochloride Liposome Injection (20 mg/10 mL and 50 mg/25 mL), a generic version of ''Doxil'', indicated for certain cancers.<ref name=":1" /> In August 2025, it obtained final approval for Tretinoin Cream USP 0.025%, equivalent to ''Retin-A'', for the treatment of acne vulgaris. During this period, the company's cumulative [[Abbreviated New Drug Application]] (ANDA) approvals from the US FDA increased from 219 to 223, including both final and tentative approvals.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alembic Pharma shares gain 2% on USFDA nod for Diltiazem Hydrochloride tablets |url=https://www.moneycontrol.com/news/business/stocks/alembic-pharma-shares-in-focus-on-usfda-nod-for-diltiazem-hydrochloride-tablets-13678512.html |website=Money Control}}</ref> These products were added to the company's portfolio in therapeutic segments such as oncology, cardiovascular diseases, dermatology, and ophthalmology.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alembic gets FDA nod for angina generic |url=https://pharma.economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/drug-approvals-and-launches/alembic-gets-fda-nod-for-angina-generic/125399409 |access-date=2025-11-18 |website=ETPharma.com |language=en}}</ref><ref name=":1" />

== Products and services ==
Alembic Pharmaceuticals manufactures and sells pharmaceutical products and active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs). Its operations include international and domestic formulations, with the latter comprising branded and generic drugs.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=Alembic Pharmaceuticals Ltd. |url=https://www.hdfcsec.com/hsl.research.pdf/Initiating%20Coverage%20-%20Alembic%20Pharmaceuticals%20-%2024%20Sep-2020.pdf |website=HDFC Securities}}</ref>

=== Therapies ===
Alembic Pharmaceuticals has operations in therapy areas, including dermatology, cardiology, gastroenterology, ophthalmology, oncology, orthopedics, anti-infectives, anti-diabetics, gynecology, and treatments for cold and cough.<ref name=":0" /> Alembic Pharmaceuticals’s API plants are cGMP-compliant and have received approvals from various international regulatory agencies. The company operates two research and development (R&D) centers and reported an investment of ₹530 crore in R&D as of 31 March 2025.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-11-11 |title=Alembic Pharma looks to expand branded portfolio, strengthen complex generics and injectables pipeline - BusinessToday |url=https://www.businesstoday.in/industry/pharma/story/alembic-pharma-looks-to-expand-branded-portfolio-strengthen-complex-generics-and-injectables-pipeline-501621-2025-11-11 |access-date=2025-11-18 |website=Business Today |language=en}}</ref>

=== Animal Health Division ===
Alembic Pharmaceuticals established its Animal Health Division in 1986. The division develops pharmaceutical products for livestock, poultry, and companion animals. Among its formulations are Sharkoferrol, an oral hematinic, Moxel Inj, a preparation of amoxicillin and cloxacillin, and injectable cephalosporins such as Xceft Inj (ceftiofur sodium) and Mceft Inj (ceftizoxime sodium).<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-05-07 |title=Alembic Pharma sees continued US growth, margin gains in animal health business - CNBC TV18 |url=https://www.cnbctv18.com/market/earnings/alembic-pharma-sees-continued-us-growth-margin-gains-in-animal-health-business-19600574.htm |access-date=2025-11-18 |website=CNBCTV18 |language=en}}</ref> In 2024, the division entered into a strategic agreement with Amlan International to distribute mineral-based feed additives for poultry health in India.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |date=2025-03-25 |title=Alembic Pharma and Amlan International partner on poultry health solutions |url=https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/companies/alembic-pharma-and-amlan-international-partner-on-poultry-health-solutions/article69373510.ece |access-date=2025-11-18 |website=BusinessLine |language=en}}</ref>
